criteria.criterion: The pushed head for athena/<job> is the job's locally landed commit (with its Athena-Job trailer and records), not the bare candidate nor the records-only commit made by work_commit/commit_with_records; the unused code is removed or justified.
criteria.evidence: In gh.rs, `landed_commit` searches the local head for the newest commit that has both `Athena-Job: <job>` and an `Athena-Verified-Content` trailer. `Athena::land_pr` passes `landed_commit(&self.git, &head, &id)` as work_commit. `work_commit` and `Git::commit_with_records` are deleted, along with their tests.

criteria.criterion: The chosen approach, rejected alternatives, and the reason (every pushed commit must pass athena check --history alone) are recorded in the design doc or decisions.md, and CHANGELOG.md is updated.
criteria.evidence: docs/decisions.md D87 and the 'What is pushed' and 'Rerun' sections of docs/design/native-pr-landing.md give the choice, three rejected alternatives and the history-check reason. CHANGELOG.md has a new Fixed entry.

criteria.criterion: When a stored PR link is open and the remote branch head differs from the fixed commit, land_pr replaces the branch head (guarded to athena/<job> only, with a lease) and reuses the same PR number, updating the stored link head; it does not open a second PR.
criteria.evidence: `refresh_head` reuses the PR, stores the new head, calls `check_replace`, and only then calls `remote.replace`. `Git::push_replace` (athena-git/src/lib.rs) is not a lease. It runs `ls-remote` and then a separate unconditional `git push remote +commit:refs/heads/branch`, so a push between the two calls is overwritten, and D87 says so ('a push by someone else between them is not excluded by git itself'). The reading specified a --force-with-lease push against the observed remote head.

criteria.criterion: The push guard still refuses any branch other than athena/<job> and any force outside the replace path.
criteria.evidence: `check_push` is unchanged and still refuses non-fast-forward pushes. `check_replace` refuses any branch other than the allowed one, and an empty branch name. `replace` is called only from `refresh_head` (open link) after `check_replace`. Tests: `the_replace_guard_allows_only_the_jobs_own_branch` and `a_rerun_never_replaces_a_branch_that_is_not_the_jobs_own`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: new unit tests in gh.rs (fake remote and host) cover the pushed commit being the landed one, rerun with an open PR replacing the head and not calling open_pr, rerun when the head already matches (no-op), and refusal for non-work branches; an athena-git test covers the lease force push.
criteria.evidence: The new tests pass: `the_pushed_commit_is_the_landing_commit_found_by_its_trailers`, `a_rerun_with_an_open_pull_request_replaces_the_head_and_reuses_the_pull_request` (opened==1), `a_rerun_whose_head_already_matches_pushes_nothing`, `a_rerun_never_replaces_a_branch_that_is_not_the_jobs_own`, plus the plain-push and merged cases. The athena-git test `push_replace_forces_only_while_the_remote_head_is_the_expected_one` passes, though what it tests is the non-atomic check (see finding).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass with no warnings.
criteria.evidence: Every test binary reported ok with 0 failed. Clippy with -D warnings finished clean. fmt --check printed nothing.

criteria.criterion: A test using a real temporary git repo with a bare remote shows the pushed branch's commits each pass the history check (trailer on governed and records changes), run via `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: `rerunning_land_pr_replaces_a_head_that_fails_the_history_check_with_the_landed_commit` in lifecycle.rs pushes the bare candidate to a bare remote and checks that check_history reports violations. It then reruns land_pr with GitRemote and checks that the remote head is the landed commit, PR 39 is kept, open_pr was not called, and check_history reports no violations. It passed.

findings.summary: The replace path uses a check-then-force push instead of an atomic lease (--force-with-lease).
findings.evidence: It runs `ls-remote --heads` and compares the result to `expected`, then runs `push remote +{commit}:{refname}`. Between the two calls the force is unconditional, and D87 admits a concurrent push is not excluded. The reading assumed `--force-with-lease` against the observed head, and criterion 3 requires a lease. Fix: `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<expected> remote <commit>:refs/heads/<branch>`.

findings.summary: An is_ancestor error is treated as 'not an ancestor', which sends the rerun to the forced replace.
findings.evidence: `job.ancestry.is_ancestor(seen, &commit).unwrap_or(false)`. If the remote head is not in the local object store, the rerun force-replaces instead of reporting the error. The branch guard still applies, but an unknown remote head is the case where an atomic lease matters most.

findings.summary: run.rs was listed as a deliverable but is unchanged; the call site lives in gh.rs.
findings.evidence: The diff touches 7 files and not run.rs. The work_commit closure in `Athena::land_pr` is updated in gh.rs, so nothing is missing.

summary: I read the full diff and ran the new targeted tests, the full `cargo test`, clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. All of them pass. The main part of the change works. `land --pr` now pushes the job's own landing commit, which it finds through the job's `Athena-Job` and `Athena-Verified-Content` trailers. `work_commit` and `commit_with_records` are removed. On a rerun with the PR open, the change reuses the stored PR, updates the stored head, and pushes nothing when the head already matches. A lifecycle test with a real bare remote shows that the bare candidate fails `athena check --history` and that the repaired branch passes it. The decision and its alternatives are recorded in D87 and in the design doc, and CHANGELOG.md is updated. The verdict is still fail because of one problem. The forced push is not protected by a lease. `Git::push_replace` reads the remote head with `ls-remote` and then runs an unconditional `+commit:ref` force push. A push by someone else between those two git calls would be overwritten, and D87 says so itself. The accepted reading asked for `--force-with-lease` against the observed head, and criterion 3 says "with a lease". The fix is small: pass `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<expected>` to `git push`. The existing test would still cover it.
